chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Art Tatum in Toledo and at the Rhythm Club (retold)
summary: Jackson recounts hearing Tatum in 1931 in Toledo and at the Rhythm Club where Fats gathered pianists; then he moves to Herman Chittison.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Then next I heard the master and that was Art Tatum. Art Tatum was playing in a little place in Toledo called Charlie's Chicken Shack.
About what year was that, Butter?
That was 1931, 1931. I was with McKinney Cotton Pickers. And when we played Toledo with the band, he used to always come around and Don would have him sit in.
Wow.
And he would sit in and play then, and I had never heard nothing like that in my life.
Uh-huh.
So he came to New York with Adelaide Hall, and I think we spoke of the rhythm club before, and he come to the rhythm club -- somebody brought him by -- and I

was there -- I happened to be there in town at the same time. And he sat down to the piano in the rhythm club and played. And Fats was there and Fats Waller went and got every piano player that he could find. He went and got the Lion.
Willie the Lion Smith, that is?
That's right, and he went and got James P. Johnson. He got all the pianists around there to come and listen to Art. And do you know not a one of them sat down and played behind Art Tatum.
I don't blame them.
And from then Fats took him and took him around New York 'cause you know Art was blind and Fats just kept him with him. And from then on they was boys.
And if you listen to any of Art's piano solos, even if for one measure, he's going to stick a measure of Fats Waller's style in there somewhere, --
Beautiful.
-- you see? Because that was his friend.
Now, he, to me, -- after you talk about Art Tatum, it's hard to talk about other pianists. I worked with a very good pianist in Zack Whyte's band, too. His name was Herman Chittison Chitizen.
Oh, yes, a very --
And when I first --
"Casey" photographer.
"Crime photographer."
He did crime on TV -- radio.
Yeah, a crime photographer. He was the incidental pianist on "crime photographer" for years.
